item.title: Suva survive tough test
item.description: SUVA may have walked away from Bidesi Ground with a convincing 52-24 victory over Lautoka in round seven of the Subrails Marama Championship yesterday, but coach Meli Tuifagalele believes the scoreline tells only half the story. item.content:encoded:
SUVA may have walked away from Bidesi Ground with a convincing 52-24 victory over Lautoka in round seven of the Subrails Marama Championship yesterday, but coach Meli Tuifagalele believes the scoreline tells only half the story.

The match report recorded a high-scoring contest, with both teams finding opportunities to cross the try line. Suva eventually pulled away to secure the win and an important bonus point, but Tuifagalele was quick to acknowledge the challenge posed by Lautoka.

“We are grateful for the win. All glory goes back to God,” Tuifagalele said.

“The result today does not reflect how hard the match was. It was actually a tough game today. The fact that we came away with a win, we are just very grateful and we will build on it in our next game.”

For Suva, the victory was about more than simply adding another win to its campaign. With the competition moving closer to the knockout stages, every point is becoming increasingly valuable, particularly for teams battling to secure favourable positions heading into the quarterfinals.

Tuifagalele said the primary objective was always to win, with the bonus point an added reward.

“Our first objective was just to get the win. The bonus point came as a bonus,” he said.

“But in the scheme of things, it is very important to get the win and also get the bonus point if ever possible.”

The Suva coach also credited the young players who have stepped up this season following the departure of several players to other provinces.

“There are a lot of young players who have stepped up this season for us,” he said. “They have really stepped up and are doing the work for us.”

However, Tuifagalele knows Suva cannot afford to become complacent.

He identified the set-piece as the biggest area requiring improvement, saying the team still needs to become more clinical. Defence is another area on his radar after the 24 points conceded against Lautoka.

“We have been trying to emphasise our defensive part of the game,” he said.

With the quarter-final race heating up, Suva has secured the points it needed. Now, Tuifagalele wants his players to turn their attacking promise into greater discipline and precision.

item.title: Nasinu’s fairy-tale chance to make history
item.description: THE 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants has reached its defining weekend with four teams left standing – and Nasinu are the unlikely side carrying the fairy-tale story into the semi-finals. The Giant Killers were not expected to be here.
item.content:encoded:
THE 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants has reached its defining weekend with four teams left standing – and Nasinu are the unlikely side carrying the fairy-tale story into the semi-finals.

The Giant Killers were not expected to be here.

They opened their campaign with a 0-1 loss to defending champions Labasa before responding with victories over Navua and Suva.

Their 2-1 victory over Suva in their final Group A match secured their place in the last four and helped send the defending champions Labasa out of the tournament.

Nasinu face Rewa at 4.30pm today at the 4R Stadium in Ba for a place in Sunday’s final.

Rewa arrive as Group B winners and have already shown they can hurt the big guns, beating Ba 3-0 in the pool stages.

But the Delta Tigers also enter the semi-final after a 0-1 loss to Nadi in their final pool match.

Ba – the most successful district in BOG history with 17 titles – face Suva in the opening semi-final at 2pm.

The Men in Black will know better than anyone what it takes to survive this stage of the competition.

But their own campaign has shown they are vulnerable.

Rewa exposed them with a 3-0 victory before Ba responded with a 3-1 win over Lautoka to secure their semi-final place.

Suva, meanwhile, topped Group A despite losing their final match to Nasinu.

For Nasinu, however, this weekend is about more than one result.

The side last reached the BOG semi-finals in 2019.

They have finished runners-up twice – in 1989 and 1991 – but have never lifted the trophy.

Two victories now stand between them and their first BOG title.

Can the Giant Killers complete the fairy-tale?

item.title: Ba chases third title
item.description: DAYALS Steels Ba president Praneel Dayal has called on the thousands of Ba supporters to rally behind the team as the Men in Black chase a place in the Extra Battle of the Giants final at home today. Ba faces Global Care Suva in the first semi-final at 2pm at 4R Stadium at Govind Park, with the Men in Black hoping to continue a remarkable season under Dayal’s leadership.
item.content:encoded:
DAYALS Steels Ba president Praneel Dayal has called on the thousands of Ba supporters to rally behind the team as the Men in Black chase a place in the Extra Battle of the Giants final at home today.

Ba faces Global Care Suva in the first semi-final at 2pm at 4R Stadium at Govind Park, with the Men in Black hoping to continue a remarkable season under Dayal’s leadership.

Ba has already secured two major titles this season, winning the Fiji FACT and the Extra Premier League, and now has its sights firmly set on a third piece of silverware.

Dayal said the team would not take its achievements for granted as it prepares for the crucial semi-final.

“We have two trophies to our name this season, but I promise you this, I take none of it for granted. Success isn’t a gift, it’s earned every single day,” Dayal said.

The Ba president said the values instilled in him by his father through the family business, Dayals Sawmillers, had shaped his approach to leadership and were now being carried into his work with the football team.

“My father’s teaching led to my own success at Dayals Sawmillers. He showed me that true success comes from relentless hard work, humility, and staying loyal to your roots.”

Those principles, Dayal said, remained at the heart of Ba as the side prepares to face a strong Suva outfit.

The occasion will also be significant for the Ba faithful, with their team playing in front of its home supporters and just one victory away from another major final.

Dayal believes the black jersey represents more than football, carrying the pride, history and identity of the Ba community.

“This badge isn’t just fabric. It’s the heartbeat of our community, our history, and our pride. When the boys step out tomorrow in that black shirt, they carry the soul of every single one of you,” he said.

With a place in the final at stake, Dayal has urged Ba supporters to make their presence felt from the stands.

“Stand loud with us tomorrow. Let’s bring this home together.” .

For Ba, the challenge is clear, defeat Suva today and take another step towards a third title in what has already been a memorable season for the Men in Black.

item.title: Defence must match attack
item.description: THE Fijiana XV are being challenged to find the same excitement without the ball as they show with it when they enter the WXV Global Series Challenger in Hong Kong. New head coach Willie Walker has stripped back the team’s game plan, focusing on the fundamentals while allowing the players to retain their natural, instinctive style.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fijiana XV are being challenged to find the same excitement without the ball as they show with it when they enter the WXV Global Series Challenger in Hong Kong.

New head coach Willie Walker has stripped back the team’s game plan, focusing on the fundamentals while allowing the players to retain their natural, instinctive style.

The Fijiana face Spain, Hong Kong China and the Netherlands in the tournament, with Walker looking to build on one win from his three Tests in charge.

“I’ve just stripped a lot of stuff back from what was previously here, and we’ve gone back to a fairly simple game plan, game style that allows our players to get into some sort of structure or some sort of shape, but still allows them to play their natural instinctive game style,” Walker said.

The coach has placed particular emphasis on the collision, carry-clean, catch-and-pass and finishing opportunities.

“We’ve created a number of opportunities, and to be honest, we’ve been disappointed with the ability to finish those chances,” he said.

Defensively, however, there are signs of progress.

The Fijiana recorded 93 per cent tackle success with only eight missed tackles last week — a significant improvement from the 43 missed tackles in their first Test against South Africa. Walker wants that improvement to become a mindset.

“We have to have the same excitement in defence that we do when we have the ball,” he said. The reason is simple.

The Fijiana’s strength is playing with the ball — so Walker wants them to win it back as quickly as possible.

item.title: Flying Fijians ready for Canada CHALLENGE
item.description: THE FIJI Water Flying Fijians will look to set the tone for their Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup campaign when they face Canada in their opening match tonight. Head coach Senirusi Seruvakula said the team was focused on starting the campaign strongly, with several players looking to make their mark in the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
THE FIJI Water Flying Fijians will look to set the tone for their Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup campaign when they face Canada in their opening match tonight.

Head coach Senirusi Seruvakula said the team was focused on starting the campaign strongly, with several players looking to make their mark in the tournament.

“It’s very important, important for the group to perform well, most of these players are from Drua,” Seruvakula said.

The Flying Fijians are also defending their Pacific Nations Cup title, but Seruvakula wants his players to focus on the task in front of them rather than the pressure of retaining the championship.

“Enjoy yourselves, play as a team,” he said.

Seruvakula acknowledged that Canada would provide a strong challenge, but said Fiji would concentrate on its own performance.

“Canada is a very good side, they have been doing well, we just focus on ourselves rather than worrying about Canada,” he said.

The match will also be an important opportunity for Seruvakula and his players, with the Flying Fijians yet to register a win under his tenure.

“This is important for us, especially these players to prove themselves, one step at a time.”

Seruvakula stressed the importance of maintaining discipline throughout the match, saying Fiji could not afford lapses in concentration.

“Discipline is important in the whole of 80 minutes,” he said.

He said the players had responded well during preparations and were enjoying their training sessions.

“Players are doing well, they enjoyed training.

“They all looking forward to this game.”

The Flying Fijians will be hoping their preparation translates into a strong performance when they meet Canada tonight.

The game will kicks off at 7pm (Fiji time)

item.title: Fireworks await fans
item.description: FOOTBALL fans can expect two exciting encounters when the semi-finals of the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants are played at Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba tomorrow. Group A winner Global Care Suva FC will face hosts Dayals Steel Ba FC in the opening semi-final at 2pm, before Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC takes on Nasinu FC at 4.30pm.
item.content:encoded:
FOOTBALL fans can expect two exciting encounters when the semi-finals of the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants are played at Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba tomorrow.

Group A winner Global Care Suva FC will face hosts Dayals Steel Ba FC in the opening semi-final at 2pm, before Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC takes on Nasinu FC at 4.30pm.

Fiji Football Association CEO Mohammed Yusuf said the four teams had earned their places in the knockout stage after an exciting three days of pool competition.

“We witnessed three days of competitive football during the pool stage, and the four best teams have qualified for the semi-finals.

“Fans can expect two thrilling matches because every team will be fighting for a place in the final.

“We encourage football supporters from around the country to come to Ba with their families and enjoy another exciting weekend of football,” Yusuf said.

Suva enters the knockout stage after recording impressive victories over Blue Gas Navua FC and defending champion Extra Supermarket Labasa FC.

Coach Pita Rabo’s side scored seven goals in its three pool matches and will now face a determined Ba side in front of its home supporters.

The Men in Black secured their semi-final berth with victories over Tagimoucia Kava Nadi FC and Khelvin Engineering Lautoka FC.

Under coach Ravinesh Kumar, Ba has already won the BiC Fiji FACT and Extra Premier League titles this season and remains in contention for a third major trophy.

The second semi-final promises another intriguing contest, with nine-time champion Rewa facing tournament surprise package Nasinu. Rewa topped Group B after convincing victories over Lautoka and Ba. The Delta Tigers will be eager to bounce back after suffering a narrow 0-1 defeat to Nadi in their final pool match.

Nasinu has been one of the tournament’s surprise packages, recovering from an opening loss to Labasa to register consecutive victories over Navua and Suva.

The Giant Killers will feature in their first BOG semi-final since 2019. With defending champion Labasa eliminated during the pool stage, a new champion will be crowned this year.

The winners of tomorrow’s semi-finals will meet in the grand final at 3pm on Sunday.

item.title: Rewa FC side wary of Nasinu
item.description: STRATUM/PPCL Rewa FC will be aiming to move a step closer to claiming its 10th Battle of the Giants title when it takes on Nasinu FC in the second semi-final tomorrow. The Delta Tigers topped Group B after securing six points from their three pool matches at Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.
item.content:encoded:
STRATUM/PPCL Rewa FC will be aiming to move a step closer to claiming its 10th Battle of the Giants title when it takes on Nasinu FC in the second semi-final tomorrow.

The Delta Tigers topped Group B after securing six points from their three pool matches at Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

Rewa opened its campaign with a 2-0 victory over Khelvin Engineering Lautoka FC before producing a dominant display to defeat hosts Dayal’s Steel Ba FC 3-0.

Despite going down 0-1 to Tagimoucia Kava Nadi FC in its final pool match, Rewa had already done enough to secure top spot and book its place in the semi-finals.

Player-coach Ratu Tevita Waranivalu will be expecting an improved performance from his players when they face a determined Nasinu side.

Rewa enters the knockout stage with plenty of experience in its squad, with several players having featured in the OFC Men’s Champions League earlier this season, where the Delta Tigers reached the semi-finals.

The side will also draw confidence from its strong domestic campaign, finishing third in the Extra Premier League.

Nasinu, however, is expected to provide a stern challenge after qualifying for its first BOG semi-final since 2019.

The Giant Killers bounced back from an opening defeat to Extra Supermarket Labasa FC by recording consecutive victories over Blue Gas Navua FC and Global Care Suva FC.

Rewa, which has won the BOG title nine times, will be determined to add another championship to its proud history.

The second semi-final between Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC and Nasinu FC kicks off at 4.30pm tomorrow at Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

item.title: Lomani ready for THE challenge
item.description: VODAFONE Fijiana XV captain Kolora Lomani is looking forward to testing Fiji’s strength against some of the world’s best women’s rugby teams in the inaugural WXV Global Series Challenger in Hong Kong. The Fijiana arrived in Hong Kong ahead of the three-week tournament, which brings together Fiji, Hong Kong China, the Netherlands, Samoa, Spain and Brazil at the Kai Tak Youth Sports Ground.
item.content:encoded:
VODAFONE Fijiana XV captain Kolora Lomani is looking forward to testing Fiji’s strength against some of the world’s best women’s rugby teams in the inaugural WXV Global Series Challenger in Hong Kong.

The Fijiana arrived in Hong Kong ahead of the three-week tournament, which brings together Fiji, Hong Kong China, the Netherlands, Samoa, Spain and Brazil at the Kai Tak Youth Sports Ground.

Fiji will open its campaign against Spain on Sunday, with Lomani expecting a tough contest against a side she knows well.

“We played against Spain in Dubai in the last WXV.

“They’re very physical and a strong team. We’re really excited for the challenge,” Lomani said.

The Fijiana will then face Hong Kong China on September 19 before completing their campaign against the Netherlands on September 26.

The tournament will feature nine international matches over three weekends, with three matches played on each match day.

For Fiji, the series provides an important opportunity to gain valuable international exposure and build momentum towards the next Women’s Rugby World Cup cycle.

The centrally hosted WXV Global Series Challenger is part of World Rugby’s evolving WXV Global Series, designed to provide more competitive matches for women’s teams while building towards the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2029.

Fiji is among 13 teams still competing for the remaining 11 places at the 2029 World Cup.

Five teams have already secured qualification, with hosts Australia joining the top four teams from the last World Cup champions England, Canada, New Zealand and France.

Eight of the remaining places will be decided through 2027 regional competitions, while two will go to the highest-ranked non-qualified teams in the World Rugby Women’s Rankings at the end of the 2027 international window.

The final place will be decided through the WXV Global Series Challenger in 2028.
